turns.user: Tin AI hôm nay có gì nổi bật?
turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là một số tin tức nổi bật về trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) trong ngày hôm nay:

1. **Thị trường cổ phiếu AI phục hồi sau biến động**
   * Các cổ phiếu ngành AI đã lấy lại đà tăng trưởng sau đợt bán tháo mạnh gần đây. Giới phân tích từ Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley và JPMorgan đều nhận định phản ứng giảm điểm của thị trường vừa qua là quá mức và hiện mở ra các cơ hội đầu tư mới, dù Nvidia vẫn chịu áp lực nhất định.
   * [Chi tiết trên Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/10/ai-stocks-nvidia-broadcom)

2. **Cảnh báo về rủi ro từ lời khuyên y tế của AI**
   * Nghiên cứu và ý kiến chuyên gia chỉ ra rằng ngay cả khi các câu trả lời y tế từ AI có độ chính xác cao, chúng vẫn có thể tiềm ẩn nguy cơ tác động tiêu cực đến hành vi của bệnh nhân do cách sắp xếp thông tin. Giới chuyên môn kêu gọi cần có các chuẩn đánh giá hành vi (behavioral benchmarking) dài hạn khi đưa AI vào giao tiếp trực tiếp với người bệnh.
   * [Chi tiết trên STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/ai-health-advice-accuracy-messaging-risk-behavioral-benchmarking)

3. **AI bị lợi dụng để tạo các cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả mạo (Swatting)**
   * Công nghệ AI đang gây khó khăn lớn cho lực lượng chức năng trong việc phát hiện các cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả. Kẻ xấu sử dụng công nghệ tạo giọng nói và tự động hóa để tạo ra các cuộc gọi báo cáo án mạng, nổ súng rất chân thực, nhằm quấy rối cơ quan hành pháp.
   * [Chi tiết trên NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/nx-s1-5971477/ai-is-making-it-harder-to-detect-fake-emergency-calls)

4. **Tâm điểm xoay quanh vị thế và thách thức của Nvidia**
   * Các phân tích tiếp tục tập trung vào vị thế thống trị của Nvidia trên thị trường chip GPU cho mô hình AI, mối quan hệ đầu tư chéo trong ngành và các áp lực địa chính trị, kiểm soát công nghệ giữa Mỹ và các đối thủ cạnh tranh.
   * [Chi tiết trên The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/why-is-nvidia-so-powerful-in-the-ai-world-and-what-could-jensen-huangs-scandal-really-cost-296257)

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Banks push online banking, then blame us when we get hacked | Opinion
items.summary:
One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] # Someone drained my bank account. Then the real nightmare began | Opinion

## Over time, AI is going to turn our brains to mush. People won't be able to remember phone numbers, basic grammar or directions to places they've visited once or twice without consulting AI overlords.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.

items.title: AI stocks bounce back — with one notable exception
items.summary:
The AI trade has regained momentum despite — or maybe because of — Nvidia's struggles following the weekend revelations from CEO Jensen Huang.

The big picture: Monday's sudden burst of exuberance for AI was the latest wide swing for a market upended by last week's "blue tsunami" in the midterm elections and the threat they could pose to the data center boom. [...] "We believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory," Goldman Sachs analysts wrote in a note Monday.
   "We believe the market's reaction to the midterms is overdone," wrote Morgan Stanley tech analysts in a note entitled "Buy the Drop: AI Investment Opportunities Post the U.S. Midterms," which it published Sunday night. [...] "We do not think AI is a continued sell here. In fact, tech drawdown is offering certain opportunities. The selloff was very sharp," JPMorgan equity strategists wrote Monday.
